title: Butter Pie
subtitle: A Lancashire shortcrust pie of potato, onion and plenty of butter
excerpt: Sliced potato and slowly cooked onion, bound in butter and baked inside a short, crumbly crust. A Friday-night pie from the Catholic communities of Lancashire.
sourceNotes: Traditional Lancashire butter pie, historically eaten on Fridays when meat was not permitted; adapted for a standard 23cm pie dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions once fully cooled. Reheat from frozen at 180C for 25 minutes, covered with foil.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pie can be assembled the night before and kept in the fridge. Bake straight from cold.

content.text: Butter pie is deliberately plain: potato, onion and butter are all it wants. Cook the onion low and slow until it is sweet, not golden. The potato slices need to be thin so they cook through inside the crust.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Melt 30g of the butter in a frying pan over a low heat. Add the onion and a good pinch of salt. Cook gently for 20 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and pale. Do not let them brown. Set aside to cool.
Par-boil the potato slices in salted water for six minutes. They should be almost tender but not breaking up. Drain and cool on a tray.
Heat the oven to 200C. Butter the pie dish lightly. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the dish, leaving a short overhang.
Layer the potato and onion into the case, seasoning each layer. Dot the remaining butter over the top layer.
Roll the rest of the pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg and lay the lid on. Press and seal the edges, then trim.
Cut two slits in the top. Brush all over with beaten egg.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the crust is golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The potato is still firm inside the baked pie.
items.cause: The slices were too thick or not par-boiled for long enough.
items.fix: Slice the potato no thicker than 5mm and ensure it is almost tender before it goes in raw.

items.cause: The filling held too much moisture.
items.fix: Drain the par-boiled potato on a clean cloth before layering. Bake on a preheated heavy baking tray.

items.symptom: The onion has a sharp taste.
items.cause: It was not cooked long enough.
items.fix: The onion needs a full 20 minutes on a low heat. Aim for pale and very soft, not browned.
